circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track that winds around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside other racing series. The venue maintains FIA Grade 1 status for international motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing reconstruction and renaming, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track situated in Azerbaijan's capital along the city's waterfront boulevard, spanning 6. 003 kilometers to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 under the European Grand Prix banner, before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix the following year.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Middle Eastern Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual F1 race alongside other motorsport events including drag racing and endurance competitions. The track, which holds an FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple configurations, has also accommodated various racing series over the years, including a stint with Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver skill. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its viewing stands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit, stretching nearly 7 km through the Ardennes region, has been a Formula One fixture since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix consistently from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as one of motorsport's most enduring championship venues.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre temporary racing facility that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international motorsport competitions including world sportscar racing, open-wheel series, and touring car championships throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has served as China's premier motorsport venue, hosting the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 until 2019 before resuming from 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing competitions alongside the Formula One event.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue located near Northamptonshire that has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948. The circuit gained further significance by hosting the inaugural round of the Formula One World Championship in 1950, though the British Grand Prix alternated between three tracks from 1955 until returning permanently to Silverstone in 1987. Beyond Formula One, the track also stages MotoGP racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the historic 1986 Hungarian Grand Prix, marking the first Formula One race held in Eastern Europe behind the Iron Curtain. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after initial plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Italy's Monza Circuit, spanning nearly 5. 8 kilometers, has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949 and remains one of only a handful of venues appearing on the Formula One calendar since the sport's beginning. Constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility, the track earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its distinctive design featuring extended straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and serves as a premier venue for international motorsport competitions. Operated by Honda Mobilityland, the track accommodates 155,000 spectators and hosts prestigious Formula One and Super Formula racing events.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, featuring the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track weaves past iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique racing venue that showcases the city's most recognizable landmarks.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honours two deceased Mexican racing drivers, the Rodriguez brothers, who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, returning to the calendar in 2015 with its current configuration, and now operates under the Mexico City Grand Prix designation since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that stretches 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and achieves average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track has hosted the Miami Grand Prix since joining the Formula One calendar in 2022, with Formula E adopting a modified version starting in the 2025–26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track winding through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, incorporating roads near Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is popularly known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout traverses that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 for the Dutch Grand Prix before concluding its partnership after 2026. The circuit earns its "Roller coaster in the Dunes" nickname from its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz that wind through the sandy terrain north of the North Sea coast.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits near the city of Lusail in northern Qatar and stretches 5. 419 kilometers with a primary straight spanning 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km racing facility in São Paulo, opened in 1940 and received its current name in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The counterclockwise track features a kart circuit bearing the name of another renowned Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit positioned along Jeddah's waterfront promenade overlooking the Red Sea, this venue has served as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its 2021 debut. The facility expanded its international racing calendar by also accommodating Formula E events starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km circuit represents a versatile test of driver skill with its combination of extended straights and diverse corner layouts. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts numerous international racing events including MotoGP and endurance competitions, while previously accommodating various other motorsport series across different categories.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British nationality who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to win both the F1 drivers' title and the world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has claimed nine race victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas in the championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in the Formula One World Championship, currently racing for the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons that included two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. He has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with Alpine, representing his country in the sport.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French racing driver currently competing for Alpine in Formula One, previously achieved a notable career victory by winning the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One competition with Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari, holding the distinction of seven world championship titles, which he shares with Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing experience from a successful endurance racing career that included a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having finished as championship runner-up in 2022. Leclerc has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW's factory team while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career. His Formula One involvement spanned two separate periods, from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024, before transitioning to his current endurance racing focus.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One drivers' title while racing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 13 race victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French motorsport professional, currently drives for Haas in Formula One competition. He previously secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while competing for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four seasons competing in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One across 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his racing career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. , a Spanish driver, currently races for Williams in Formula One after competing in the series for 12 seasons and securing four race victories during his career.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously campaigned in IMSA's LMP2 division.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for the 2026 season, supporting both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One while racing for Red Bull Racing, where he has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, having participated in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently works as a reserve driver for the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Based in Enstone, this Formula One operation has competed under the Alpine name since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works team to showcase its sports car division. The squad maintained its factory status through Renault's involvement before the automotive manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has established itself as a recurring presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the modern iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the Formula One racing arm of the Italian luxury car manufacturer, holds the distinction of being both the longest-running and most accomplished team in the sport's history. Competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950, the team is recognized by its iconic "Prancing Horse" emblem and remains a cornerstone institution in Formula One racing.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American-licensed Haas Formula operates as a Formula One entry founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas in 2014, debuting on the grid in 2016. Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who led the outfit since its inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, this Swiss engineering firm competed as an independent Formula One constructor from 1993 onwards, becoming the fourth-longest-running team in the sport's history before ceasing operations in 2025. Prior to its F1 involvement, the company achieved notable success in endurance racing, including a 1989 Le Mans victory alongside Mercedes-Benz. The team's assets and operations were purchased by Audi in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's works Formula One program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with Mumtalakat Holding Company as its parent owner.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current iteration based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The team, now jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff since 2022, competes as Mercedes-AMG Petronas. The marque's racing efforts are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister squad in Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that commenced competition in 2024, operating as a sister squad to Red Bull Racing under the Red Bull GmbH ownership structure. Headquartered in Faenza with operations extending to Milton Keynes, the team functions as one of two Red Bull-owned constructors in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England that has been owned by Red Bull GmbH since its establishment in 2005. The squad was led by Christian Horner throughout its entire history until 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal. Red Bull GmbH also operates Racing Bulls as its second Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of the sport's established operations.
